headline: Medium-risk pair: Perplexity can feed unverified web-derived content into Rasa, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct shared filesystem is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity performs live web search and browsing, so it can surface attacker-controlled text; Rasa is a customer-support bot that ingests dialogue text. No shared filesystem or MCP bridge is documented, but the pairwise pathway from Perplexity outputs into Rasa inputs is plausible in default integrations, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is copied or forwarded into Rasa training or runtime messages
IF Rasa rules or NLU treat external text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a human review step before any Perplexity text enters Rasa
Strip markup and instruction-like phrases from imported text
Use a fixed prompt/template boundary for Rasa inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from Perplexity to downstream messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while Rasa handles text and voice. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, same OAuth principal, or automatic file sharing, so leakage is not evidenced beyond a manual bridge. Because the interaction is undocumented and both are closed/open mixed, I keep this low.
conditions: IF uploaded documents from Perplexity are manually pasted into Rasa logs or tickets
IF Rasa is configured to persist conversation transcripts containing sensitive text
mitigations: Avoid copying uploaded documents into Rasa transcripts
Redact secrets before handoff
Set short transcript retention in Rasa
requires-engineering: isolate Perplexity and Rasa workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and Rasa is only documented with allowlisted network egress plus messaging APIs. No overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource is documented, so a capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF a shared database or git repo is added outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only to shared artifacts
Separate storage paths per agent
Disable any shared mutable mount
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is optimized to generate cited answers from web search, and Rasa is a dialogue system that can act on user messages. If Perplexity output is forwarded into Rasa without verification, Rasa may treat it as authoritative. The profiles do not prove this default, but the pathway is credible enough to rate medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Perplexity answers are inserted into Rasa responses or intents without review
IF Rasa downstream actions are triggered by those imported answers
mitigations: Require source verification before Rasa acts on Perplexity text
Add confidence thresholds for imported facts
Log and review all cross-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: implement citation-aware validation

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and touches uploaded documents and browsing context; Rasa is open-source with allowlisted egress and messaging integrations. The profiles do not show a residency, retention, or certification mismatch for the same regulated data class, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Perplexity into Rasa channels with different retention settings
IF an operator stores EU or PHI data in both systems without a DPA or residency review
mitigations: Classify data before cross-system use
Align retention settings across both systems
Block regulated data from unsupported channels
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA controls
